The regionalization is not about reorganization, including merger, consolidation, annexation, nor does it mandate districts participate in particular activities under a regional plan. The New York State Education Department website goes on to say, there is not a one-size-fits-all approach to creating opportunities for students. New York State's educational landscape already features many different examples of partnerships across schools and districts, as well as existing regional infrastructure that offers support, such as cross-district contracts and Board of Cooperative Educational Services, commonly known as BOCES. The outcomes and action items from regional planning conversations will vary from region to region, building upon the strengths inherent in local communities and reflecting innovative ideas from the individuals who live in them. Thus far, the district has been asked to complete a strengths and needs tool provided by the New York State Education Department to determine the types of efforts we are engaged in here in Irvington, including information about our portrait of a graduate and supports that may be needed to improve student opportunities.
